title: Perfectness of a flat finite-type polynomial quotient
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a flat finite-type homomorphism of commutative Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and let $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$ be a polynomial presentation [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Then $A$, regarded as a $P$-module through the presentation, is a perfect $P$-complex [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]: it admits a bounded resolution by finitely generated projective $P$-modules [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. In addition, $A$ has finite Tor dimension over $R$, meaning that there are integers $a\le b$ such that $H^i(A\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M)=0$ for every $R$-module $M$ in degree zero and every $i\notin[a,b]$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Derived tensors here are ordinary module derived tensors, computed on K-flat first complexes as in [lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model].

source.place: Tags 067J, lemma-flat-finite-presentation-perfect, and 068Y, lemma-perfect-ring-map; the Noetherian finite-type case in dualizing.tex Tag 0BZW, lemma-relative-dualizing-algebraic.

proof.text: The map $R\to P$ is of finite type: the identity presentation $R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow P$ has kernel zero, including $n=0$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes $P$ Noetherian. If $\pi:P\twoheadrightarrow A$ is the given presentation, then for each $a\in A$ choose $f\in P$ with $\pi(f)=a$; one has $a=f\cdot1$. Hence $A$ is a cyclic, in particular finitely generated, $P$-module, and $A[0]$ is bounded with finite terms.

source.place: Tag 00FN, algebra-lemma-Noetherian-permanence; the polynomial chart in Tag 068Y.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], $A$ is flat over $R$ via the given map $\varphi:R\to A$. The presentation $\pi:P\twoheadrightarrow A$ is an $R$-algebra map, so its restricted module action is $r\cdot a=\pi(r\cdot1_P)a=\varphi(r)a$. Thus [lem-trf-base-flat-polynomial-tor-bound] applies to $M=A$. It gives $\operatorname{Tor}^P_j(A,N)=0$ for every $P$-module $N$ and $j>n$. It also identifies $A[0]\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L[0]$ with $(A\otimes_RL)[0]$ for every $R$-module $L$. This degree-zero complex has zero cohomology in every other degree, proving the finite-Tor assertion over $R$ with $a=b=0$.

source.place: Tags 068X (lemma-perfect-over-polynomial-ring), 0658 (lemma-perfect), 066Q (lemma-perfect-module), assembled on the given polynomial presentation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-module-tor-projective-resolution] with $S=P$, $M=A$ and $d=n$. Step 1 gives its Noetherian and finite-generation hypotheses; Step 2 gives its ordinary first-variable Tor hypothesis for every $P$-module. The resulting $E^\bullet\simeq A[0]$ has finitely generated projective terms and support in $[-n,0]$, so [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex] gives perfectness. For $n>0$, the stated augmentation and exactness equations give $0\to E^{-n}\to\cdots\to E^0\to A\to0$: at the left endpoint, $\ker d_E^{-n}=\operatorname{im}d_E^{-n-1}=0$ because $E^{-n-1}=0$. For $n=0$, the cited augmentation is an isomorphism $E^0\cong A$, giving the resolution $0\to E^0\to A\to0$.
